inputs.original_text: Concerns are mounting over proposed changes to Cyprus’ surveillance legislation, particularly efforts to remove judicial oversight as a key safeguard, lawyers said on Monday. The amended bill is expected to be brought before the House plenum for a vote on Thursday. According to Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides, following a recent closed session of the House [...]
inputs.modified_text:
Folks, we are witnessing yet another assault on traditional order and constitutional safeguards right now in Cyprus. The political establishment is aggressively rushing dangerous changes to surveillance legislation through the system, with the amended bill expected to be brought before the House plenum for a vote on Thursday. 

On Monday, lawyers rightly raised alarms about these alterations to judicial oversight. This entire scheme is being rammed through behind closed doors, away from public scrutiny. As Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides pointed out following a recent closed session of the House, this underhanded behavior tells you everything you need to know about whose interests the ruling class is really protecting. 

When the administrative state operates in secret and strips away proper channels, it undermines the stability and trust that keep a society functioning. We must stand up for traditional accountability and resist these backdoor maneuvers that threaten our constitutional norms and basic public order.
